answer_justification.hook: AGMARK = DMI India (1937 law). FAO = UN body founded 1945. No connection.

1635.trap_explanation: Students may doubt S2 (PM appointing QCI chair on industry recommendation) as unusual or constitutionally odd — it is, in fact, QCI's deliberate PPP design where industry nominates the chair.

statements.text: QCI was set up jointly by the Government of India and the Indian Industry
statements.reason: QCI (1997) was jointly established by Ministry of Commerce & Industry and apex industry bodies (CII, FICCI, ASSOCHAM) as a PPP quality institution.

statements.text: Chairman of QCI is appointed by the Prime Minister on the recommendations of the industry to the Government
statements.reason: This PM-appointment-on-industry-recommendation process is QCI's actual governance design — reflecting its PPP character.

answer_justification.fact: Both correct: QCI = joint Govt+Industry body (S1); Chairman appointed by PM on industry recommendation (S2) → (c).
answer_justification.elimination_path: S1 unambiguous. S2 unusual but accurate — PPP design where industry nominates, PM appoints. Both true → (c).
answer_justification.hook: QCI PPP model: Govt + Industry create it; industry nominates chair; PM appoints.

1636.trap_explanation: Students may doubt S2 (DIPP as IP nodal agency) thinking DIPP handles only industrial investment/licences — its expanded post-2016 mandate includes IP regime oversight and National IPR Policy implementation.

statements.text: It reiterates India's commitment to the Doha Development Agenda and the TRIPS Agreement
statements.reason: National IPR Policy (2016) explicitly reaffirms TRIPS obligations while emphasising Doha Development flexibilities for public health.

statements.text: Department of Industrial Policy and Promotion is the nodal agency for regulating intellectual property rights in India
statements.reason: DIPP (now DPIIT) is designated the nodal department for National IPR Policy implementation and IP administration oversight.

answer_justification.fact: Both correct: National IPR Policy (2016) reiterates TRIPS/Doha (S1); DIPP/DPIIT is nodal for IP (S2) → (c).
answer_justification.elimination_path: S1 confirmed by policy text. S2: DIPP's IPR mandate formalised in National IPR Policy 2016. Both true → (c).
answer_justification.hook: DIPP → DPIIT: nodal for both industrial investment AND intellectual property.

1637.trap_explanation: NITI Aayog is India's apex planning body — students may assume NIIF falls under it. S2's ₹4,00,000 crore is a 10x inflation of the actual corpus, testing numerical precision under time pressure.

statements.text: It is an organ of NITI Aayog
statements.reason: NIIF is set up by the Ministry of Finance as a Category II Alternative Investment Fund — structurally independent of NITI Aayog.

statements.text: It has a corpus of Rs. 4,00,000 crore at present
statements.reason: NIIF's target corpus is ~₹40,000 crore (₹20,000 crore government + matching private). ₹4,00,000 crore is 10x the actual figure.

answer_justification.fact: NIIF = Ministry of Finance Category II AIF (not NITI Aayog). Corpus ~₹40,000 crore, not ₹4,00,000 crore. Both false → (d).
answer_justification.elimination_path: S1: NIIF is under MoF, not NITI Aayog. S2: ₹4 lakh crore = 10x actual ~₹40,000 crore. Both anchors wrong → (d).
answer_justification.hook: NIIF = MoF Category II AIF. Corpus ~₹40,000 crore — not 4 lakh crore.

1638.trap_explanation: S1 inverts the legal test — 'owner unaware' is NOT a PBPT exemption. S3 inverts the appellate structure — the Act DOES establish an Appellate Tribunal. Both are designed to sound like reasonable legal provisions.

statements.text: A property transaction is not treated as a benami transaction if the owner of the property is not aware of the transaction
statements.reason: PBPT Act defines benami by beneficial ownership separation — not owner awareness. Exemptions apply to spouse/children/HUF coparceners, not unawareness.

statements.text: Properties held benami are liable for confiscation by the Government
statements.reason: PBPT Act 1988 (amended 2016) explicitly empowers confiscation of benami properties by Initiating Officer/Adjudicating Authority.

statements.text: The Act provides for three authorities for investigations but does not provide for any appellate mechanism
statements.reason: PBPT Act establishes both an Adjudicating Authority AND an Appellate Tribunal — an appellate mechanism clearly exists.

answer_justification.fact: S2 ✓ (confiscation). S1 ✗ (awareness ≠ exemption). S3 ✗ (Appellate Tribunal exists) → (b) 2 only.
answer_justification.elimination_path: S1: exemptions = spouse/child/HUF, not unawareness. S3: Appellate Tribunal in PBPT Act contradicts 'no appellate mechanism'. Only S2 survives.
answer_justification.hook: PBPT: confiscation ✓, unawareness exemption ✗, Appellate Tribunal ✓ — S1 and S3 both inverted.

2137.trap_explanation: S2 (fungal infections) inserts a plausible-sounding ecological harm that has no causal link to butterflies — students may accept it without recognising butterflies play no role in fungal pathogen suppression.

statements.text: Pollination of some plants could be adversely affected
statements.reason: Butterflies are important pollinators for many flowering plants; population fall reduces pollination services for butterfly-dependent species.

statements.text: There could be a drastic increase in the fungal infections of some cultivated plants
statements.reason: Butterflies have no documented role in controlling fungal pathogens of plants. Fungal infections are controlled by soil microbes, not butterfly populations.

statements.text: It could lead to a fall in the population of some species of wasps, spiders and birds
statements.reason: Butterflies and caterpillars are prey for wasps, spiders, and insectivorous birds — population fall triggers trophic cascade upward.

answer_justification.fact: Butterfly decline: pollination loss (S1) + trophic cascade to predators (S3). No butterfly-fungal pathogen link → S2 false → (c).
answer_justification.elimination_path: S1 = pollinator function. S3 = prey item in food chain. S2 = fabricated butterfly-fungus link. Eliminate options with S2.
answer_justification.hook: Butterflies = pollinators + prey. No role in fungal suppression.

2183.trap_explanation: Bhitarkanika (saltwater crocodile territory) and Deepor Beel (Assam wetland) are both reptile/wildlife-rich sites that could plausibly host gharials — students unfamiliar with gharial's river-specific habitat may choose them.

answer_justification.fact: Gharials (Gavialis gangeticus) are confined to deep, fast-flowing rivers — best remaining wild population is in National Chambal Sanctuary.
answer_justification.elimination_path: Bhitarkanika = mangroves + saltwater crocodiles, not gharials. Pulicat = coastal lagoon. Deepor Beel = Assam wetland, Gangetic range. Chambal = correct.
answer_justification.hook: Gharial = Chambal. Saltwater croc = Bhitarkanika. Mugger = everywhere in peninsular rivers.

distractor_analysis.reason: Bhitarkanika is known for saltwater crocodiles, not gharials — different species, different habitat.
Pulicat Lake is a coastal lagoon in AP — not a fast-flowing river habitat suitable for gharials.
Deepor Beel is an Assam wetland/Ramsar site — outside the Gangetic plains gharial range and habitat type.

2264.trap_explanation: S2 inverts bioremediation's limitation for heavy metals — 'readily and completely treated' is false because heavy metals (Cd, Pb) cannot be biodegraded, only sequestered or bioaccumulated.

statements.text: It is a technique for cleaning up pollution by enhancing the same biodegradation process that occurs in nature
statements.reason: Bioremediation accelerates natural microbial degradation of organic pollutants — it is nature-based pollution remediation.

statements.text: Any contaminant with heavy metals such as cadmium and lead can be readily and completely treated by bioremediation
statements.reason: Heavy metals are non-biodegradable. Bioremediation can only sequester or bioaccumulate them — 'readily and completely treated' overstates the technique.

statements.text: Genetic engineering can be used to create microorganisms specifically designed for bioremediation
statements.reason: Engineered bacteria (e.g., Deinococcus radiodurans for radioactive sites, Pseudomonas variants) are established in bioremediation research.

answer_justification.fact: S1 ✓ (natural biodegradation enhancement). S2 ✗ (heavy metals not biodegradable — only sequestered). S3 ✓ (GMO bioremediation) → (c).
answer_justification.elimination_path: S2 is the trap: heavy metals like Pb and Cd are elements — microbes cannot degrade them, only bind/immobilise. S1 and S3 are standard bioremediation facts.
answer_justification.hook: Bioremediation degrades organic pollutants. Heavy metals = non-degradable — only stabilised.

2265.trap_explanation: 'Oxygen demand' pulls students toward blood oxygen (SpO₂) or altitude oxygen — the 'biological' qualifier and the 'standard criterion' framing point specifically to water quality assessment, not physiological oxygen.

answer_justification.fact: BOD = Biological Oxygen Demand = measure of organic pollutant load in water bodies; standard metric for aquatic pollution severity.
answer_justification.elimination_path: (a) Blood oxygen = SpO₂/PaO₂ in clinical settings. (b) Forest oxygen = photosynthesis/respiration balance. (d) Altitude = partial pressure. BOD = aquatic pollution → (c).
answer_justification.hook: BOD = mg O₂/L over 5 days at 20°C — water quality test, not physiological.

distractor_analysis.reason: Blood oxygen levels are measured by pulse oximetry (SpO₂) or arterial blood gas (PaO₂), not BOD.
Forest ecosystem oxygen balance uses net ecosystem productivity measurements, not BOD.
High-altitude oxygen levels relate to atmospheric pressure, measured by barometry — not BOD.

2303.trap_explanation: Students may accept coal seams and depleted reservoirs while doubting deep saline formations (S3) as an unfamiliar option — but saline aquifers have the largest global carbon storage capacity.

statements.text: Abandoned and uneconomic coal seams
statements.reason: CO₂ injected into coal seams displaces adsorbed coalbed methane — a proven enhanced CBM recovery and sequestration technique.

statements.text: Depleted oil and gas reservoirs
statements.reason: Depleted reservoirs have proven geological traps; CO₂ enhanced oil recovery (CO₂-EOR) also sequesters carbon.

statements.text: Subterranean deep saline formations
statements.reason: Deep saline aquifers have the largest theoretical global CO₂ storage capacity — brine-bearing porous rock formations.

answer_justification.fact: All three are proven geological carbon sequestration sites: coal seams, depleted reservoirs, and deep saline formations → (d).
answer_justification.elimination_path: S1 and S2 are the known options. S3 (deep saline) is the most important globally by volume. All three → (d).
answer_justification.hook: Deep saline formations = largest CO₂ storage globally. All three sites are IPCC-endorsed.

2334.trap_explanation: Students may be uncertain about wild buffalo or Indian wild ass being in Schedule I — both are rare enough to warrant highest protection, though they are less iconic than gharial.

statements.text: Gharial
statements.reason: Gharial is in Schedule I of WPA 1972 — highest protection; critically endangered with <200 adults remaining.

statements.text: Indian wild ass
statements.reason: Indian wild ass (Equus hemionus khur), confined to Rann of Kutch, is Schedule I — cannot be hunted except under law.

statements.text: Wild buffalo
statements.reason: Wild buffalo (Bubalus arnee), found in Chhattisgarh/Assam, is Schedule I under WPA 1972.

answer_justification.fact: All three — gharial, Indian wild ass, wild buffalo — are Schedule I of WPA 1972, granting highest protection against hunting → (d).
answer_justification.elimination_path: Gharial = iconic Schedule I. Indian wild ass (Rann of Kutch) = Schedule I. Wild buffalo (Chhattisgarh/Assam) = Schedule I. All three → (d).
answer_justification.hook: All three are Schedule I — highest WPA protection alongside tiger, lion, rhino.

concept_hooks: gharial Indian wild ass wild buffalo

2335.trap_explanation: 'M-STrIPES' has 'stripes' suggesting tigers but the abbreviation is unfamiliar; option (a) 'captive breeding' and option (c) 'satellite navigation' are plausible guesses from the letters M/S.

answer_justification.fact: M-STrIPES = Monitoring System for Tigers — Intensive Protection and Ecological Status; NTCA app for tiger reserve patrolling.
answer_justification.elimination_path: (a) Captive breeding = CCMB/Zoo programmes, not M-STrIPES. (c) Satellite navigation = NAVIC/GPS. (d) Highway security = NHAI/police. (b) = tiger reserve monitoring.
answer_justification.hook: M-STrIPES = tiger patrol app used by NTCA forest guards in tiger reserves.

distractor_analysis.reason: Captive breeding programmes for wild fauna are managed separately by CCMB and national zoological institutions.
Indigenous satellite navigation = NavIC (formerly IRNSS), a ISRO project — unrelated to M-STrIPES.
National highway security uses NHAI/police infrastructure, not M-STrIPES.

2336.trap_explanation: Options b/c/d describe specific biological or conservation statuses — students may conflate Schedule I with extinction status or endemism, when it simply means maximum legal protection parity.

answer_justification.fact: Schedule I of WPA 1972 = highest legal protection. A tortoise in Schedule I enjoys identical statutory protection as the tiger (also Schedule I).
answer_justification.elimination_path: (b) 'No longer exists in wild' = Critically Endangered/Extinct — not what Schedule I means. (c) Endemism is a biogeographic fact, not a Schedule I implication. (d) Combines b+c, both wrong. (a) = correct.
answer_justification.hook: Schedule I = maximum protection parity — tortoise = tiger, legally.

distractor_analysis.reason: Schedule I does not mean extinct in wild — it means cannot be hunted. Many Schedule I animals exist in wild populations.
Endemism is a biogeographic characteristic, not a consequence of Schedule I classification.
Combines (b) and (c), both incorrect — Schedule I implies protection level, not extinction or endemism.

2337.trap_explanation: Corbett, Mudumalai, and Sariska are prominent wildlife sanctuaries — all plausible lion translocation sites. Only Kuno Palpur (MP) was specifically designated by the SC for lion translocation from Gir.

answer_justification.fact: SC 2013 ordered translocation of Asiatic lions from Gir (Gujarat) to Kuno Palpur Wildlife Sanctuary (MP) as a second home.
answer_justification.elimination_path: Corbett = tigers/elephants, Uttarakhand. Mudumalai = TN, on WG, not designated. Sariska = tiger reserve, Rajasthan. Kuno Palpur = SC-ordered second lion home.
answer_justification.hook: Kuno Palpur = Asiatic lion second home, SC order 2013. (Later used for cheetah 2022 — context is 2017 lion plan.)

distractor_analysis.reason: Corbett National Park is a tiger reserve in Uttarakhand — not considered for Asiatic lion translocation.
Mudumalai is a tiger/elephant reserve in Tamil Nadu — not the designated lion translocation site.
Sariska is a tiger reserve in Rajasthan — not designated for lion translocation.

2338.trap_explanation: Nallamala (EG), Nagarhole (WG), and Seshachalam (EG) are all ecologically significant forests — but none serves as an EG-WG bridge. Only Sathyamangalam spans the Nilgiri-Eastern Ghats junction.

answer_justification.fact: Sathyamangalam Tiger Reserve (Tamil Nadu) forms the ecological corridor linking Bandipur-Mudumalai (Western Ghats) to Eastern Ghats via Nilgiri-Eastern Ghats junction.
answer_justification.elimination_path: Nallamala = Eastern Ghats AP only. Nagarhole = Western Ghats Karnataka only. Seshachalam = Eastern Ghats AP only. Sathyamangalam = the EG-WG bridge.
answer_justification.hook: Sathyamangalam = Nilgiri junction corridor = EG-WG ecological bridge.

distractor_analysis.reason: Nallamala Forest is in the Eastern Ghats (AP) and does not extend to the Western Ghats.
Nagarhole is a Western Ghats forest (Karnataka) — it is part of the WG cluster, not the EG-WG link.
Seshachalam Biosphere Reserve is in the Eastern Ghats (AP) — not a WG-EG corridor.

2393.trap_explanation: WRI and WBCSD are credible-sounding climate research bodies that could plausibly coordinate GCCA — students may accept S3 without knowing GCCA is coordinated by the EU Commission directly.

statements.text: It is an initiative of the European Union
statements.reason: Global Climate Change Alliance was launched by the EU in 2007 as an EU Commission initiative for climate-development integration in vulnerable developing countries.

statements.text: It provides technical and financial support to developing countries to integrate climate change into their development policies
statements.reason: GCCA's stated purpose is integrating climate change adaptation and mitigation into development plans of most vulnerable developing countries.

statements.text: It is coordinated by World Resources Institute (WRI) and World Business Council for Sustainable Development (WBCSD)
statements.reason: GCCA is coordinated by the EU Commission itself — WRI and WBCSD are separate private climate research organisations with no GCCA coordination role.

answer_justification.fact: S1 ✓ (EU initiative). S2 ✓ (climate-development integration for vulnerable countries). S3 ✗ (EU Commission coordinates GCCA, not WRI/WBCSD) → (a).
answer_justification.elimination_path: S1+S2 confirmed by GCCA mandate. S3: WRI/WBCSD are US-based private organisations — no coordination role in an EU initiative.
answer_justification.hook: GCCA = EU Commission initiative. WRI/WBCSD = separate private bodies, not GCCA coordinators.

2394.trap_explanation: S1 inverts CCAC's founding structure — 'G20 initiative' sounds plausible (G20 has climate mandates) but CCAC was a multi-stakeholder UNEP-led coalition, not a G20 exclusive initiative.

statements.text: Climate and Clean Air Coalition (CCAC) is a unique initiative of G20 group of countries
statements.reason: CCAC was launched in 2012 by 6 founding countries + UNEP as a multi-stakeholder coalition — not a G20 initiative. It includes many non-G20 members.

statements.text: The CCAC focuses on methane, black carbon and hydrofluorocarbons
statements.reason: CCAC specifically targets Short-Lived Climate Pollutants (SLCPs): methane, black carbon, HFCs, and tropospheric ozone.

answer_justification.fact: CCAC = multi-stakeholder UNEP-led coalition (not G20). S2 correct: focuses on methane, black carbon, HFCs → (b).
answer_justification.elimination_path: S1: 'G20 initiative' is wrong — CCAC is a voluntary multi-country coalition outside G20. S2: SLCPs (methane/BC/HFCs) is correct scope.
answer_justification.hook: CCAC = Short-Lived Climate Pollutants coalition (UNEP + countries), not G20.

2395.trap_explanation: TRAFFIC monitors wildlife trade — UNEP (also wildlife-focused) is a plausible institutional home. Students may accept S1 without knowing TRAFFIC is actually a joint IUCN+WWF programme founded 1976.

statements.text: TRAFFIC is a bureau under United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP)
statements.reason: TRAFFIC is a joint programme of IUCN and WWF founded in 1976 — it has no formal institutional relationship with UNEP.

statements.text: The mission of TRAFFIC is to ensure that trade in wild plants and animals is not a threat to the conservation of nature
statements.reason: TRAFFIC's stated mission is monitoring wildlife trade to ensure it does not threaten wild species' conservation — including CITES implementation.

answer_justification.fact: TRAFFIC = IUCN + WWF joint programme (not UNEP). Mission correctly described in S2 → (b).
answer_justification.elimination_path: S1: UNEP runs CITES Secretariat, not TRAFFIC. TRAFFIC = IUCN+WWF since 1976. S2 = standard TRAFFIC mission statement.
answer_justification.hook: TRAFFIC = IUCN + WWF. CITES Secretariat = UNEP. Distinct bodies.

2455.trap_explanation: S1 inverts algae biofuel production geography — 'only in seas' is false because photobioreactors and freshwater ponds on land are the primary production systems used globally.

statements.text: Production of algae based biofuels is possible in seas only and not on continents
statements.reason: Algae biofuels are produced in land-based photobioreactors and open raceway ponds — 'seas only' is an inversion of actual production systems.

statements.text: Setting up and engineering algae based biofuel production requires high level of expertise/technology
statements.reason: Algae cultivation, lipid extraction, and fuel conversion at scale require specialised biotechnology infrastructure — a genuine developing-country constraint.

statements.text: Economically viable production necessitates large scale facilities which may raise ecological and social concerns
statements.reason: Large open pond systems require land and water; potential for contamination and displacement of existing land uses raises ecological/social issues.

answer_justification.fact: S1 ✗ (algae grown on land in photobioreactors, not only seas). S2 ✓ (high technology requirement). S3 ✓ (large-scale concerns) → (b).
answer_justification.elimination_path: S1: algae biofuel industry uses land-based PBRs and ponds — 'seas only' is wrong. S2 and S3 are real documented limitations.
answer_justification.hook: Algae biofuel = land photobioreactors + open ponds. Not seas-only.

1732.trap_explanation: S1 substitutes 'Eastern Pacific Ocean' (ENSO/El Niño domain) for the correct 'Eastern Indian Ocean' — a deliberate ocean-basin swap that sounds plausible because students associate Pacific with climate anomalies.

statements.text: IOD is characterised by a difference in sea surface temperature between tropical Western Indian Ocean and tropical Eastern Pacific Ocean
statements.reason: IOD = SST difference between tropical Western Indian Ocean and tropical EASTERN INDIAN Ocean — not Eastern Pacific. Eastern Pacific = ENSO domain.

statements.text: An IOD phenomenon can influence an El Niño's impact on the monsoon
statements.reason: Positive IOD (warm WIO, cool EIO) can partially offset El Niño's suppressive effect on Indian monsoon — documented modulation.

answer_justification.fact: IOD = Western Indian Ocean vs Eastern Indian Ocean SST difference. S1 wrong (Pacific, not Indian Ocean). S2 correct → (b).
answer_justification.elimination_path: S1: 'Eastern Pacific' is ENSO (El Niño), not IOD. IOD = within Indian Ocean. S2 = established IOD-monsoon interaction. Only S2 correct.
answer_justification.hook: IOD = Indian Ocean Dipole. Both poles are in the Indian Ocean — not Pacific.

concept_hooks: SST sea surface temperature Indian Ocean

1808.trap_explanation: Students may miscount by skipping a state or confuse Jharkhand/Bihar as necessary route states — the minimum-state route via Nagaland-Assam-WB-Odisha-AP-TN-Kerala gives exactly 7.

answer_justification.fact: Minimum route: Nagaland (Kohima) → Assam → West Bengal → Odisha → Andhra Pradesh → Tamil Nadu → Kerala (Kottayam) = 7 states.
answer_justification.elimination_path: Count including origin+destination: Nagaland(1) Assam(2) WB(3) Odisha(4) AP(5) TN(6) Kerala(7). No state can be skipped on this minimum-border route.
answer_justification.hook: Kohima→Kottayam: 7 states. N-A-WB-O-A-T-K.

distractor_analysis.reason: 6 states would require skipping one border state — no valid road route bypasses all 7 on this N-S traverse.
8 states would mean traversing through an additional state like Jharkhand or Telangana — not the minimum.
9 states is further from minimum; no route needs this many states for Kohima to Kottayam.

1809.trap_explanation: Borneo, Java, and Sri Lanka are all large islands in the Indo-Pacific region — students may pick Sri Lanka (on the 'Indian side') or Java (large, prominent) without knowing Great Nicobar's proximity to Sumatra's northern tip.

answer_justification.fact: Great Nicobar (southernmost A&N island) is ~163 km from Aceh, Sumatra (Indonesia) via the Six Degree Channel.
answer_justification.elimination_path: Sri Lanka = across BoB, ~1500 km NW. Borneo = far east, beyond Strait of Malacca. Java = SE of Sumatra, much farther. Sumatra = 163 km via Six Degree Channel.
answer_justification.hook: Great Nicobar → Sumatra (Aceh tip): Six Degree Channel, ~163 km.

distractor_analysis.reason: Borneo is east of Sumatra, across the Strait of Malacca — much farther from Great Nicobar.
Java lies southeast of Sumatra; it is significantly more distant from Great Nicobar than Sumatra's north tip.
Sri Lanka is northwest of the Andaman & Nicobar chain across the Bay of Bengal — roughly 1500+ km away.

1886.trap_explanation: S1 falsely co-locates Teesta's and Brahmaputra's origins — both rise in the eastern Himalaya but from different watersheds. S3 falsely ends Teesta at the Bay of Bengal when it actually joins the Brahmaputra in Bangladesh.

statements.text: The source of river Teesta is the same as that of Brahmaputra but it flows through Sikkim
statements.reason: Teesta originates from Pauhunri/Gurudongmar Lake, Sikkim. Brahmaputra originates from Chemayungdung Glacier, Tibet. Different source regions.

statements.text: River Rangeet originates in Sikkim and it is a tributary of river Teesta
statements.reason: Rangeet (or Rungeet) originates in the Singalila Range of Sikkim and joins Teesta at Triveni/Teesta-Rangeet confluence.

statements.text: River Teesta flows into Bay of Bengal on the border of India and Bangladesh
statements.reason: Teesta does not reach the Bay of Bengal directly — it merges with the Brahmaputra (Jamuna) in northern Bangladesh before reaching the sea.

answer_justification.fact: S1 ✗ (different sources — Sikkim vs Tibet). S2 ✓ (Rangeet tributary in Sikkim). S3 ✗ (joins Brahmaputra in Bangladesh, not BoB directly) → (b).
answer_justification.elimination_path: S1: Teesta = Gurudongmar Lake, Sikkim; Brahmaputra = Chemayungdung, Tibet. S3: Teesta → Brahmaputra (Bangladesh). Only S2 survives.
answer_justification.hook: Teesta: Gurudongmar Lake (Sikkim) → WB → Bangladesh → Brahmaputra. Not Bay of Bengal directly.

1921.trap_explanation: Bhavnagar (Gulf of Khambhat, Gujarat) also has extreme tidal range — students familiar with Khambhat tides may pick it. Chandipur (Odisha) is the specific 'vanishing sea' phenomenon where the sea floor is walkable.

answer_justification.fact: Chandipur (Balasore, Odisha) = 'hide-and-seek beach' — sea recedes ~5 km exposing the seafloor twice daily due to gentle intertidal slope.
answer_justification.elimination_path: Bhavnagar (Gulf of Khambhat) has large tidal range but not walkable seafloor exposure. Bheemunipatnam/Nagapattinam = Tamil Nadu/AP coasts. Chandipur = specific phenomenon.
answer_justification.hook: Chandipur = Odisha 'vanishing beach.' Near DRDO missile test range, Balasore.

distractor_analysis.reason: Bhavnagar (Gulf of Khambhat, Gujarat) has extreme tidal range but the seafloor exposure at Chandipur is the specific named phenomenon.
Bheemunipatnam is near Visakhapatnam, AP — no specific tidal seafloor exposure phenomenon documented there.
Nagapattinam is a Tamil Nadu coastal town — no comparable tidal seafloor-walkable phenomenon.

1961.trap_explanation: S2 (gypsum) sounds like a soil amendment that could improve water retention — but gypsum specifically addresses sodic soil (calcium replaces sodium), not water conservation. Students may accept all three as 'good agricultural practice'.

statements.text: Reduced or zero tillage of the land
statements.reason: Reduced/zero tillage preserves soil structure and organic matter, reducing evaporation from the topsoil and retaining moisture.

statements.text: Applying gypsum before irrigating the field
statements.reason: Gypsum (calcium sulphate) treats sodic/alkaline soils by replacing sodium — its purpose is soil reclamation, not water conservation.

statements.text: Allowing crop residue to remain in the field
statements.reason: Crop residue mulch reduces soil surface evaporation, conserves soil moisture, and improves infiltration — a proven water conservation practice.

answer_justification.fact: S1 ✓ (no-till retains moisture). S2 ✗ (gypsum = sodic soil reclamation, not water conservation). S3 ✓ (mulch reduces evaporation) → (c).
answer_justification.elimination_path: S2 is the trap: gypsum targets soil chemistry (sodium → calcium exchange), not water storage. S1 and S3 directly reduce evaporation.
answer_justification.hook: Gypsum = sodic soil fix. For water conservation: no-till + crop residue.

2082.trap_explanation: Jordan and Iraq are Middle Eastern nations with sea access, making them plausible Mediterranean border countries — students may not recall that Jordan's coast is the Gulf of Aqaba (Red Sea) and Iraq's is the Persian Gulf.

statements.text: Jordan borders the Mediterranean Sea
statements.reason: Jordan's only sea access is a short Gulf of Aqaba coastline (Red Sea arm) at Aqaba — it has no Mediterranean coast.

statements.text: Iraq borders the Mediterranean Sea
statements.reason: Iraq's coast is on the Persian Gulf (Shatt al-Arab/Basra area) — it has no Mediterranean coastline.

statements.text: Lebanon borders the Mediterranean Sea
statements.reason: Lebanon has an entirely Mediterranean coastline running through Beirut, Tyre, Sidon — Mediterranean is Lebanon's western border.

statements.text: Syria borders the Mediterranean Sea
statements.reason: Syria has a northwest Mediterranean coastline (Latakia region) — a relatively short but real Mediterranean frontage.

answer_justification.fact: Jordan = Gulf of Aqaba (Red Sea). Iraq = Persian Gulf. Lebanon + Syria = Mediterranean. → (c) 3 and 4 only.
answer_justification.elimination_path: Jordan: Aqaba = Red Sea. Iraq: Basra = Persian Gulf. Lebanon: Beirut = Mediterranean. Syria: Latakia = Mediterranean. Only 3+4 → (c).
answer_justification.hook: Jordan-Aqaba=Red Sea. Iraq-Basra=Persian Gulf. Lebanon+Syria=Mediterranean.

concept_hooks: Jordan Gulf of Aqaba Red Sea
